original_question: Fix ε > 0 and an integer r > 1. Determine whether there exists a finite group G whose invariant ms(G, r), the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of G, is smaller than ε.
correct_elements: Your draft has identified the right open problem: it asks whether, for fixed ε and r, one can find a finite group G for which the normalized guaranteed size of a monochromatic symmetric subset, ms(G,r), is arbitrarily small. It also correctly understands ms(G,r) as a worst-case guarantee over all r-colorings, not as the size achieved by a particular coloring. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
missing_details: The paper’s notion of a symmetric subset in an arbitrary group must be stated explicitly: a subset A ⊆ G is symmetric if A = gA^{-1}g for some g ∈ G (equivalently, A is invariant under the symmetry x ↦ gx^{-1}g).
The paper defines first MS(G,r), then the normalized quantity ms(G,r) = MS(G,r)/|G|; the draft mentions only ms(G,r) informally.
The official definition of MS(G,r) is as the least upper bound of all cardinals t such that every r-coloring χ:G→{1,…,r} contains a monochromatic symmetric subset A with |A| ≥ t.
The question is about arbitrary finite groups, not only Abelian groups.
The exact quantifier structure should be explicit: for every ε > 0 and every integer r (your r > 1 captures the nontrivial regime), does there exist some finite group G with ms(G,r) < ε?
To be fully stand-alone, 'monochromatic' should be tied to the coloring map χ, i.e. χ is constant on A.
The paper notes that this is asked specifically in Section 4 as a finite-group invariant question and that it is related to Theorem 1.5.
refined_question: Fix ε > 0 and an integer r ≥ 2. For a finite group G, let MS(G,r) be the least upper bound of all t such that every r-coloring χ:G→{1,…,r} contains a monochromatic subset A ⊆ G with |A| ≥ t and A = gA^{-1}g for some g ∈ G; equivalently, A is symmetric with respect to the group symmetry x ↦ gx^{-1}g. Define ms(G,r) = MS(G,r)/|G|. Does there exist a finite (not necessarily Abelian) group G such that ms(G,r) < ε?
justification: This is exactly the finite-group question posed in Section 4. The paper first defines, for finite groups, the invariant MS(G,r) and its normalized version ms(G,r), then asks in Question 4.4 whether for every ε > 0 and every r there exists a finite group G with ms(G,r) < ε. The surrounding context is the contrast between positive lower bounds for Abelian and odd-order groups and the even-order counterexample ms(Q8,2) = 1/8 < 1/4; immediately before Question 4.4 the authors say that this question is related to Theorem 1.5. The draft was already very close, but to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful one must add the group-theoretic definition of 'symmetric subset' and the formal definition of ms(G,r) via MS(G,r). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
